To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
loss of CF AP251, an axonemal protein located on the inner surface adjacent to DNAH 1, causes immotile spermatozoa lacking mitochondria in men.

loss of the calmodin- and radial-spoked-associated complex protein CFAP251, which is encoded by the WDR66 gene, results in spermatozoa lacking flagellum and mitochondrial sheath and infertility in men.

we have identified CFAP251 as a new gene causing male infertility in humans, which is involved in the biogenesis of sperm flagella and is required for the formation of the mitochondrion sheath in sperm flagella.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and characterization of a novel human infertility gene.
the discovery and functional characterization of CFAP251 as a novel component of the sperm flagellum and the first axonemal protein identified to date in men with isolated asthenozoöspemia.
the identification of the molecular cause of asthenozoosperemia and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of sperm flagella biogenesis in humans.

CFAP251 mutations lead to immotile spermatozoa lacking mitochondria and infertility in men.
CFAP251 loss-of-function mutations lead to immotile spermatozoa with a flagellum lacking mitochondria and that this causes infertility in men.
loss of CF AP251 leads to immotile spermatozoa lacking mitochondria and infertility in men.

CFAP251 loss leads to immotile spermatozoa lacking mitochondria and infertility in men.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the axoneme of the sperm flagellum is a highly conserved structure, and that mutations affecting the axoneme can lead to asthenozoos spermatozoa, even when they are not accompanied by morphological abnormalities.
CFAP251 loss of function is associated with asthenozoospermy, and we propose that CFAP 251 should be considered for genetic testing in men with isolated asthenozoopermy.
